text:
maria: Quick post with live experiment notes — ran a small bench targeting PyTorch/CUDA allocator knobs under our KV-cache heavy chat workload (seq=1024, bursty open requests). Observed a repeating sawtooth OOM pattern correlated with split-size + expandable_segments combos. TL;DR below.

jonathan: Can you drop the repro command and the minimal logs?

maria: Repro command I used:```bash
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.1,max_split_size_mb:32,expandable_segments:1 python perf_repro/kv_burst.py --seq 1024 --qps 120 --duration 300
```logs (trimmed):```
[EPOCH 23] alloc 1.2GB -> 1.4GB delta
[EPOCH 24] cuda OOM at allocate 256MB, freeing 3 buffers -> retry success
[EPOCH 25] alloc jumps 900MB -> 2.1GB (sawtooth)
Traceback (most recent call last): RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 134217728 bytes
```

lee: Saw this pattern before. The allocator grows segments then GC doesn't free enough contiguous region, so large downstream allocations hit OOM even though total free looks sufficient. Did you capture fragmentation numbers? :thinking: 

maria: I computed a crude fragmentation metric (free_noncontiguous / total_free). Example table from 3 runs:```
config                    | p99(ms) | OOMs | total_allocs | frag_ratio
expandable=1, split=32, gc=0.10 | 180     | 4    | 1523         | 0.68
expandable=0, split=32, gc=0.10 | 150     | 0    | 1470         | 0.21
expandable=1, split=64, gc=0.05 | 165     | 1    | 1498         | 0.47
```
Notes: expandable=1 with small split tends to create many small segments that fragment under KV eviction patterns.

ashley: Frag ratio definition please — how are you measuring contiguous vs total free?

maria: simple snapshot: walk free list, merge contiguous ranges, sum sizes. contiguous_free = sum(merged), total_free = sum(all entries). frag_ratio = 1 - (contiguous_free/total_free). It's noisy but correlates here.

zack: Two quick ideas: 1) buffer reuse patch (hot-reuse by size class) I prototyped in rx-alloc branch reduces churn; 2) kernel selection interaction — when max_split_size_mb is low the runtime chooses a different matmul kernel path that temporarily allocs a larger workspace (observed with profiler). That extra workspace often triggers the big alloc that fails.

maria: Good point on kernel selection. Profiler trace shows this:```
[profile] op matmul: kernel chosen=hybrid_im2col (workspace 280MB) when split<=32
[profile] op matmul: kernel chosen=fast_gemm (workspace 80MB) when split>=48
```So ironically increasing split (less splitting) picked fast_gemm and reduced peak workspace.

jonathan: So maybe the fix is hybrid: set expandable_segments=0 to avoid many tiny segments, bump max_split_size_mb to 48 or 64, and lower garbage_collection_threshold so GC triggers earlier and coalesces? Suggest: expandable=0, split=64, gc=0.05. Can you run that? @maria

perf-bot: Perf run started: r=kv-burst/exp-64-gc-5 (link: https://ci.internal/runs/kv-burst/456). Baselines auto-collected.

maria: Ran jonathan's suggestion:```bash
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.05,max_split_size_mb:64,expandable_segments:0 python perf_repro/kv_burst.py --seq 1024 --qps 120 --duration 300
```Results: p99=142ms, OOMs=0, frag_ratio=0.18. No sawtooth. Latency improved too. Will push a short experiment PR with the buffer-reuse patch + these knob defaults for further CI runs. :thumbsup:

lee: Nice. One extra ask — can we capture kernel selection decision in our traces (emit chosen_kernel tag) so future perf diffs can explain sudden memory cliffs?

maria: Agree. I'll add a small trace point in the runtime to log kernel path per op and attach to perf artifacts. Also will run the buffer-reuse patch with these spacings and open a follow-up thread for rollout plan (canary, A/B).

zack: If we go with default change, note this might slightly affect throughput for very short sequences (fast_gemm vs im2col tradeoff). We'll add a perf guardrail in console to auto-fallback by route.

maria: Plan: 1) small PR with knob defaults + trace tags 2) buffer-reuse patch (rx-alloc branch) 3) run full suite across seqs [128,512,1024,2048] 4) canary on staging Dedicated. Will post PR links here when ready.

jonathan: Thanks — good actionable triage.

perf-bot: Perf run finished: r=kv-burst/exp-64-gc-5 -> p99 down 18% vs baseline, no regressions flagged. (details in CI) :tada:

maria: Sweet. I'll open PRs today and ping infra for a canary window.
